name: Claude Code Philly
description:
## Claude Code Saturdays 🤖💻

**A weekly hands-on meetup for builders using Claude to write, refactor, and reason about code.**
Claude Code Saturdays is a relaxed, collaborative session for developers, founders, and tinkerers who want to explore what’s possible with Anthropic’s Claude for real-world coding tasks. Whether you’re prototyping a new app, improving an existing codebase, or just experimenting with AI-assisted development, this meetup is a space to learn by doing.

### What to Expect

* 🧑‍💻 **Live coding & pair-building** with Claude
* 🔍 **Prompting techniques** for better code generation and refactoring
* 🧠 **Reasoning-heavy tasks**: debugging, architecture, tests, and docs
* 🚀 **Show & tell**: share what you’re building or stuck on
* ☕ **Casual, friendly atmosphere**—bring your laptop and curiosity

### Who Should Attend

* Software engineers (any level)
* Startup founders and indie hackers
* Students learning to code with AI
* Anyone curious about AI-assisted development with Claude

You don’t need to be an expert—just a willingness to experiment and learn together.

### What to Bring

* A laptop
* A project, idea, or problem (optional but encouraged)
* Access to Claude (or just come observe and discuss)

Let’s spend our Saturdays building smarter, faster, and more thoughtfully—with Claude as our coding companion.
👉 **RSVP and join us for Claude Code Saturdays!**

name: Adapting Your Data Strategy for AI
description:
***PLEASE REGISTER ON THE [WEBSITE](https://damaphila.starchapter.com/meetinginfo.php?id=50&ts=1782589865) TO OBTAIN ACCESS TO THE BULDING AND TO PAY FOR YOUR TICKET.***

Breakfast and lunch are included.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the industry, and successful AI needs a strong data foundation. When building your Data Strategy, it can be challenging to balance when to embrace AI and when the foundational aspects of data management, business intelligence, and data governance come into play. This presentation will include how to balance both innovation and foundation with practical, business-focused approaches to building an effective strategy and roadmap.
Topics include:

* Prioritizing AI and Analytics Use Cases
* Aligning AI with Data Management and Data Governance
* Building the Right Team - Roles and Responsibilities
* Developing an Effective Roadmap

**Donna Burbank** will be speaking on this topic. A recognized industry expert in data management with over 25 years of experience helping organizations enrich their business opportunities through data. She is currently the Managing Director of Global Data Strategy, Ltd., where she assists organizations around the globe in driving value from their data. Donna speaks regularly at industry conferences, she has co-authored several books on Data Management, and is a regular contributor to industry publications.
**Securing Your Data for AI**
**Session Description**
AI changes what enterprise data does. Beyond reporting and analytics, data now directly shapes model behavior, retrieval, recommendations, automation, and agent actions — making data governance a security concern. This session uses LLM04 2026: Data and Model Poisoning as an industry reference point to examine how poisoning risk enters through untrusted sources, manipulated content, stale knowledge, unsafe feedback loops, and AI-accessible data that is treated as more authoritative than it should be. The session will connect these risks to the governance controls required to secure data for AI systems.
**Additional Topics**

* How AI expands the enterprise data attack surface
* How poisoned or manipulated content affects RAG retrieval and recommendations
* How compromised fine-tuning sets and feedback loops degrade model behavior
* Source trust, provenance, and authority for AI-accessible data
* Ingestion controls and lifecycle management for AI pipelines
* Vulnerability identification and testing specific to AI data flows
* Mapping LLM04 2026 to practical data governance decisions

**Mark Roxberry** will be speaking on the topics. He is a trusted consultant in AI security and intelligent systems architecture with over 20 years of experience helping organizations navigate the intersection of data, risk, and emerging AI. He is Principal Consultant for Security and Intelligent Solutions at Database Solutions Inc. and holds CISSP and CEH certifications. Mark works with clients across healthcare, gaming, financial services, and other regulated industries. He leads the OWASP HACTU8 AI security testing project and the OWASP LLM04 Working Group, speaks regularly on AI governance and secure architecture, and focuses on making enterprise AI capabilities useful, testable, and governable in production environments.

name: OG Coffee&Code Coding!
description:
# ☕ The OG Coffee&Code Meetup

### A Blockspace Community × Coffee&Code Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”
This is **The OG Coffee&Code**—the meetup that started it all, now presented in collaboration with the **Blockspace Community**.
No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

## What this meetup is

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

## What this meetup is not

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

## How it works

1. Show up
2. Grab coffee ☕
3. Open your laptop, notebook, or sketchpad
4. Work at your own pace
5. Chat when you want and focus when you need
6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

## Who should attend

* Software engineers and data professionals
* Students and self-learners
* Founders and indie hackers
* Designers, tinkerers, and technologists
* Members of the Blockspace and Coffee&Code communities
* Anyone who enjoys building things with other humans

Whether this is your first Coffee&Code, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.
This collaboration brings together two communities around a shared goal: creating a relaxed, supportive space where people can build, learn, and connect.

**Come for the code.**
**Stay for the community.**
**Leave caffeinated. ☕🚀**

description:
Join us for the 14th Philadelphia Hardware Meetup! Come join us to hear from our guest speakers as well as share what’s on your desk. We always have time for an open mic.

***[Please click here to RSVP on Luma!](https://luma.com/qxtaofeu)***

​​​This time, we're back at **Delve's** office on Arch Street.

​*Hardware Meetups happen across 30+ cities monthly and help bring together different professionals to connect and meet each other.*

​**We will have a great set of featured speakers for the evening!:**

* ​[Dan Lykens](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlykens/?utm_source=luma), Electromechanical Engineer at [Production Systems Automation](https://www.psasystems.com/?utm_source=luma). Dan is a multidisciplinary engineer and entrepreneur with over a decade of experience in electromechanical systems, PCB design, and product development. At PSA, he leads defense-focused R&D projects, specializing in rugged electronics. Dan combines deep technical proficiency in PCB design, CAD modeling, and advanced prototyping techniques.
* ​[David Levine](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-j-levine/), Senior Solutions Engineer, [Viam](https://viam.com). Viam is a software platform for building, deploying, and managing robotics applications. Viam brings software engineering practices to robotics: version control, remote monitoring and diagnostics, staged rollouts, and a registry of modules and models you can build on. At Viam, David is one of the leaders of robotic solution design -- including hardware, electronics, safety systems, and supporting software -- for automation customers across various industries. Prior to joining Viam, David received his Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from UPenn in 2023 and B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Cornell in 2017, and previously founded a robotics startup in the Philadelphia ecosystem, which was later supported by the Cornell Tech Runway Postdoctoral Fellowship.
* [Daniel Marcq](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daniel-marcq-jr/), Client Partner and Senior Director of Electrical & Software Engineering at [Delve](http://www.delve.com/). Dan leads the development of complex hardware and connected systems from early strategy through commercialization. Since joining Delve in 2019, he has led multidisciplinary programs spanning electrical engineering, embedded systems, robotics, sensing, controls, and software for medical devices and other advanced products.

​**Thank you to our partners!:**

​We’re excited to welcome **[Efinix](https://www.efinixinc.com/index.html?utm_source=luma)** as a sponsor of our next Philadelphia Hardware Meetup!
Efinix manufactures the world’s most efficient FPGAs. Delivering low power, high performance and small physical size, Efinix FPGAs offer fast time to market in a cost-effective footprint. Efinix offers three families of FPGAs from the entry level Trion family that prioritizes I/O and connectivity to the Titanium family that offer high speed transceivers and high compute capability for industrial, edge and highly accelerated AI applications. The portfolio spans 4,000 logic elements up 375,000 logic elements and includes SiP offering with Flash and system memory in the same FPGA package. These highly integrated solutions reduce design complexity, increase available I/O and further speed time to market. The Efinix Efinity tool suite is freely available and delivers an intuitive RTL to bit-stream capability while supporting a rich IP library and software compilers for the suite of Sapphire RISC-V processors available as both hard IP and soft macros across the Efinix portfolio.
Efinix FPGAs have been widely adopted in a broad array of markets from industrial automation , communications, medical, automotive and test and measurement. To find out more about Efinix products and markets, visit [www.efinixinc.com](http://www.efinixinc.com/ "http://www.efinixinc.com").
Thank you to Efinix for supporting the Philadelphia hardware community and helping bring local engineers, founders, and product developers together.

​[Ben Franklin Technology Partners](https://benfranklin.org/?utm_source=luma), our food sponsor for the evening. BFTP creates and retains highly paid, sustainable jobs by investing in and linking early-stage technology firms and established manufacturers with experts, universities, follow-on funding, and other resources to help them prosper through innovation.

​[Delve](http://www.delve.com/?utm_source=luma), our hosts AND drink sponsors for the evening, are a multidisciplinary product innovation and development firm that brings bold ideas to market. For 55 years, Delve has mobilized the best experts and technologies for our clients. And along the way, we've earned 1,500 patents and 200 design awards.

name: Hiring Talent and Getting Hired in an AI-Driven Market
description:
Join fellow ProductTank members and a panel of career and recruiting experts from Computer Enterprises, Inc. for a conversation about how AI is reshaping the hiring process from both sides of the table.

Whether you’re a hiring manager trying to understand how the candidate experience and talent landscape are changing, a product professional navigating your own career, or simply curious about how AI is influencing recruiting and hiring, you’ll come away with new perspectives and practical takeaways.

***Some of the areas we’ll explore:***

* How AI is changing the job search and candidate hunt
* Using AI for resumes, LinkedIn profiles, and interview preparation
* What recruiters are paying attention to
* How hiring managers might evolve their hiring process
* How candidates can stand out in a crowded market
* What AI can help with and where human judgment still matters
* Common misconceptions about recruiting and AI
* How recruiters are using AI today, including some of CEI’s experiences and lessons learned

***Event Info:***

* **When:** Wednesday, October 7th, 2026
* **Time:** 6:00-8:30 PM ET
* **Location:** CEI Plymouth Meeting Office
* **Address:** **[660 W Germantown Pike](https://www.google.com/maps/search/660+W+Germantown+Pike?entry=gmail&source=g),** Suite LL100, Plymouth Meeting, PA 19462

***Event Schedule:***

* **6:00–6:30 PM:** Networking
* **6:30–7:30 PM:** Panel discussion and Q&A
* **7:30–8:30 PM:** Networking and farewell

***About Our Partner & Sponsor****:*
CEI is an AI platform engineering firm that helps organizations build and scale digital products, modernize technology platforms, and unlock value from data and AI. We partner with enterprise teams across product, engineering, data, and technology to accelerate innovation, improve delivery, and bring new capabilities to market faster. In addition to our engineering and consulting services, CEI helps organizations attract, hire, and retain top technology talent through specialized recruiting and workforce solutions. By combining technology expertise with talent solutions, CEI helps organizations move from strategy to execution and achieve measurable business outcomes.

***About Our Panelists:***
Our ProductTank Organizer Joshua Aversa will moderate the conversation between:

* **Matthew Linneman**
*VP, Key Accounts & Recruiting, CEI*
Matthew Linneman is Vice President of Key Accounts & Recruiting at CEI, where he has spent more than 16 years helping organizations build high-performing technology teams and scale strategic client partnerships. Throughout his tenure, he has held leadership roles spanning sales, staffing, recruiting, and business development, and today leads CEI’s recruiting and key account organizations with a focus on talent strategy, growth, and innovation.

* **Matthew Pribbernow**
*Senior Team Lead, CEI*
Matthew Pribbernow is a Senior Team Lead at CEI with nearly 10 years of experience helping organizations attract, hire, and retain top technology talent. He leads recruiting initiatives across a wide range of technical disciplines and partners closely with both hiring leaders and candidates to build teams that support innovation and business growth.

* **Katie Dougherty**
*Senior Professional Recruiter, CEI*
Katie Dougherty is a Senior Professional Recruiter at CEI with more than five years of experience helping technology professionals connect with opportunities that align with their skills and career goals. She works closely with both candidates and hiring managers and brings firsthand insight into today’s evolving technology job market, hiring trends, and candidate expectations.

We hope you’ll join us for a practical and candid conversation about navigating the increasingly AI-influenced product talent market!

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

name: RSVP to the next Philly RHUG!
description:
**REGISTER HERE: [https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)**

In recent months, AI has fundamentally reshaped cybersecurity. Automated tooling now discovers open-source vulnerabilities and generates exploits at unprecedented speeds. As the sheer volume and velocity of CVE disclosures overwhelm traditional workflows, IT and security teams face a daunting challenge: How do you patch rapidly without destabilizing mission-critical production environments?
Join us for the next [Philadelphia Red Hat User Group (RHUG)](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451) to explore how Red Hat turns the tide on AI-driven threats by securing the software supply chain from code to deployment.
What we'll cover:

* Red Hat Trusted Libraries: How cryptographically signed, SLSA-compliant binaries neutralize upstream risks before code hits production.
* Project Lightwell: How automated, validated patching and backports maintain enterprise stability in an AI-accelerated threat landscape.
* Peer Networking: Connect with local IT leaders and Red Hat experts over food and drinks at Philly's newest high-energy venue.

[Event Details:](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)

* Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
* Time: 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM ET
* Location: F1 Arcade Philadelphia \| 1330 Chestnut St\, Philadelphia\, PA 19107

Don't miss this opportunity to transform your security posture while networking with industry peers.
Have questions? Reach out to us at rhug@redhat.com.
We look forward to seeing you there!
Best regards,
The Red Hat User Group Team
